files.content:
PLANT FORENSIC AUDIT — WHITEFIELD FACILITY
Audit Lead: Quality & Safety Inspection Team
Subject: Failure Rate Spike in Production Batch #B-8802
Findings: Out of 84 AMR-1000 units manufactured in August 2026 under Batch #B-8802, exactly 35 units (41.6% failure rate) suffered emergency thermal shutdowns within 72 hours of customer deployment.
Thermal telemetry revealed motor controller logic boards suffered voltage overload, triggering emergency battery cutoffs.

Thermal Sensor Event Log:
Unit #B8802-04: Voltage spike on MCU bus at 14:22:01 -> MCU board temperature hit 114°C -> Emergency Battery Cutoff Triggered.
Close-up forensic laboratory photo showing charred C-402 MCU board with blown voltage regulation capacitors.

folders.name: SUPPLIER
folders.description: Component procurement logs and vendor compliance audits

files.content:
CONFIDENTIAL SUPPLIER INVESTIGATION REPORT
Target Vendor: Apex Electronics (Supplier ID: VEND-992)
Component Supplied: C-402 Microcontroller Unit (MCU Board)
Audit Discovery: Due to a global semiconductor shortage in July 2026, procurement authorized an uncertified shipment of 200 C-402 MCU boards from vendor Apex Electronics.
Lab examination confirmed Apex Electronics delivered counterfeit / non-automotive grade microcontrollers that lacked surge protection capacitors. Under sustained 48V motor loads, the chips leaked voltage into the thermal management bus, causing severe battery overheating shutdowns.
Vendor Liability: Apex Electronics knowingly substituted sub-spec microcontrollers without engineering change notices (ECN). Total direct financial damage: ₹2.4 Million (₹24,00,000).

DEKRA INDEPENDENT SEMICONDUCTOR LAB AUDIT
Subject: Microcontroller Batch C-402 from Apex Electronics
Conclusion: Sub-standard consumer grade silicon repackaged with forged automotive grade laser markings.
Microscopic side-by-side comparison photo of genuine Infineon MCU vs counterfeit Apex Electronics C-402 board showing missing surge protection capacitors.

From: procurement@aurarobotics.in
To: cfo@aurarobotics.in
Subject: Urgent MCU Component Authorization for Batch B-8802

CFO,
Our primary supplier Infineon has a 6-week delivery delay on MCU logic chips. Vendor Apex Electronics offered immediate delivery of 200 units of "equivalent" C-402 microcontrollers at a 15% discount. We waived the 14-day lab burn-in test to meet Amazon's delivery deadline.

Reply from CFO:
Approved on emergency basis, but ensure vendor Apex Electronics warrants full indemnity for defect losses.

Slack Transcript #quality-emergency:
[Aug 05 10:14] QualityTech: "Hey team, the Apex MCU boards don't have the secondary capacitor footprint on C4."
[Aug 05 10:16] ProcurementLead: "Ship them anyway, CFO signed the emergency waiver for Batch B-8802."

EXECUTIVE BOARD BRIEFING — INCIDENT B-8802
Total loss capped at ₹2,400,000. Full recovery proceedings initiated against Apex Electronics.
Draft Press Briefing: Aura Robotics proactively replaces 35 units under customer warranty SLA.
